transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

E18 typically indicates a drainage issue where the machine couldn't empty the water in time. The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter or drain hose, though it could also be related to the household waste plumbing. To help us narrow this down safely, please switch off and unplug the machine first. Then, check if you can hear the pump humming when it tries to drain during that cycle.
Ok, I've switched it off and unplugged it. Before that, when it tried to drain I could hear a hum from low down at the front, otherwise it was quiet. No burning smell. What should I check next?

That humming sound suggests the pump is trying to work but might be blocked or struggling. The most likely cause for E18 with these symptoms is something caught in the pump filter, such as a coin or hair grip. To check this safely, place some towels on the floor in front of the machine and open the small flap at the bottom left. Slowly unscrew the filter to see if water drains out and if you can find any debris blocking it.

Ok, I've put towels down and opened the flap. Water's still in the drum though, so should I use the little emergency drain hose first before unscrewing the filter? Floor is tiled so it's easy to get at the front.

You don't need to use the emergency drain hose first because it is designed specifically to help you access the filter when water blocks the way. Since your floor is tiled, just place a shallow tray or some towels under the flap and unscrew the filter slowly; this will let the water out safely into your container. The E18 code usually points to a blockage in that filter area, so clearing it might resolve the issue entirely. Once the water has drained, check if there is any debris caught in the pump impeller behind the filter.
Ok, I'll unscrew the filter slowly over a tray and towels. I'll let you know what I find.

That sounds like a good plan. Once you've cleared any debris from the filter and ensured the pump impeller turns freely, please screw it back in tightly. Then, plug the machine back in and run a drain or spin-only programme to see if the water empties correctly this time. Let me know how that test goes so we can decide on the next step.

Found a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round the filter, plus a lot of fluff. The impeller turned slightly notchy then free. I put it back, plugged in and ran a drain/spin, and it drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spins normally. The floor got a little wet while I was draining it, but there's no water near the socket.

That is excellent news! It sounds like clearing out that sock and fluff has completely resolved the drainage issue. To help prevent this from happening again, I would recommend checking the filter regularly and making sure to empty your pockets before washing clothes.
